content.title: About
content.content: Chestnuts are the edible fruits of chestnut trees (Castanea spp.) that grow in temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere. The nuts have a sweet, slightly nutty flavor and a soft, buttery texture after cooking. Chestnuts are usually boiled, roasted, or baked and are used in desserts, soups, and side dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chestnut trees belong to the beech family and are more closely related to oaks than to true nuts.
Raw chestnuts contain high levels of tannins, making them bitter; heat treatment removes the bitterness.
Chestnuts have been an important food source in Europe and Asia since ancient times.
In Japan, chestnut paste (kuri kinton) is a traditional sweet, while in Italy roasted chestnut puree is a common spread.
Chestnut trees can live for several centuries and produce nuts for up to 200 years.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Chestnuts provide vitamin B6, thiamine, and folate, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Their high starch content offers a steady source of energy with a relatively low glycemic index.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike most nuts, chestnuts contain very little fat, making them suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Chestnuts contain vitamin C and polyphenols that help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chestnuts, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Tannin content
items.content: Raw chestnuts contain tannins that can irritate the stomach; they should always be cooked before consumption.

items.title: Possible contaminants
items.content: Chestnuts harvested near roads may contain pollutants; thorough washing and peeling are recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chestnuts are typically boiled in salted water for 20‑30 minutes, then peeled of their outer shell and inner skin. They can be roasted, baked, added to soups, pureed, used in desserts, or ground into chestnut flour for baking. Roasted chestnuts are a popular winter snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh chestnuts in the refrigerator in an airtight container for 1‑2 weeks. Dried roasted chestnuts keep best in a cool, dry place in a sealed bag for up to 3 months.

content.title: About
content.content: Grits are finely ground corn kernels designed for quick preparation. This version is cooked only with water, without milk or butter, making it a convenient low‑calorie breakfast.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Grits originated in the Southern United States as a staple of Native American cuisine.
Corn, the base of grits, is one of the oldest cultivated crops in the Americas.
Instant grits are often fortified with B‑vitamins and iron.
Traditionally grits are served with cheese, butter, or seafood, but this version is prepared solely with water.
Grits are easily digestible and suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Rich in complex carbohydrates
items.content: Grits provide sustained energy and help keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The water‑only preparation contains minimal fat, fitting well into low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Corn grits contain fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains iron and vitamin B6
items.content: These micronutrients are important for blood formation and metabolism.

items.title: Hypoallergenic
items.content: Grits rarely cause allergic reactions unless a person is allergic to corn.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may be allergic to corn products.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Grits can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Lack of fat
items.content: The fat‑free preparation may reduce absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins unless they are added later.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pour boiling water (about 200 ml) over the grits, cover, and let stand for 3–5 minutes. Optionally season with salt, herbs, chopped vegetables, or a spoonful of low‑fat cottage cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the package in a dry, cool place away from moisture and direct sunlight. After opening, keep the bag tightly sealed to prevent moisture absorption.

hot-dog-sandwich-beef-on-white-bun.title: Hot Dog Sandwich, Beef, on White Bun

content.title: About
content.content: The hot dog sandwich with beef on a white bun is a classic fast‑food item: a juicy beef sausage, grilled or boiled, placed inside a soft white bun. It is commonly served with mustard, ketchup, mayonnaise, and pickles.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first hot dog appeared in the United States in the late 19th century and quickly became an icon of street food.
Traditionally the sausage is made from beef, though some regions mix beef with pork.
White buns are usually baked without seeds to let the meat flavor shine.
In the US, July 23 is celebrated as National Hot Dog Day.
There are more than 30 topping variations, from classic mustard to exotic options like pineapple or fried onions.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Beef sausage provides about 12 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Beef is rich in heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies vitamin B12 and niacin, important for energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: A hot dog delivers quick calories, useful during periods of high physical activity.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: The combination of protein, fat, and carbohydrates makes the meal filling and helps control appetite.

items.title: High saturated fat
items.content: Beef sausages can contain up to 10 g of saturated fat per 100 g, which may increase cardiovascular risk if consumed frequently.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Sausages are often salty; excess sodium can contribute to elevated blood pressure.

items.title: Preservatives and nitrites
items.content: Nitrites are added to preserve color and shelf life; high intake is considered potentially harmful.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The white bun is made from wheat flour, making the product unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Hot dogs are typically eaten hot, the bun split lengthwise, and topped with desired sauces and condiments. Serve with French fries, coleslaw, or pickled vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store sausages in the refrigerator at +2–4 °C, no more than 3 days after opening the package. Keep buns in a dry place in a sealed bag, or freeze for up to 3 months for longer storage.

potato-boiled-from-fresh-peel-not-eaten-.title: Potato, boiled, from fresh, peel not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Boiled potato is a cooked tuber of fresh potato, prepared without added fat. The peel is not consumed, so it is removed before or after boiling. The potato has a soft texture, neutral flavor, and serves as a base for many dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potatoes were introduced to Europe from South America in the 16th century.
There are more than 4,000 potato varieties differing in colour, shape, and taste.
Boiled potatoes retain most of their vitamin C when not overcooked or stored too long.
Potato skin is rich in fiber and nutrients, but in this product the peel is not eaten.
Potato is one of the most widely consumed root vegetables worldwide.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Boiled potatoes provide slowly digestible carbs that give lasting satiety.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids iron absorption.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports normal heart function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When boiled without added oil, potatoes contain virtually no fat, making them suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Even without the peel, the flesh provides a modest amount of fiber beneficial for digestion.

items.title: Solanine content
items.content: Green or sprouted potatoes may contain toxic solanine; such potatoes should be discarded.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to potatoes.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Boiled potatoes can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boiled potatoes can be eaten plain, diced into salads, used in mashed potatoes, soups, and casseroles. They store well in the refrigerator for 3‑4 days.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store boiled potatoes in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. Do not leave them at room temperature for more than 2 hours to prevent bacterial growth.

content.title: About
content.content: Water, Enhanced, Diet is purified drinking water enriched with vitamins, minerals, and low‑calorie natural flavorings. It is designed to maintain hydration while providing beneficial micronutrients without added sugar.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Enriched with vitamin C and vitamin B12 to support immunity and energy.
Mineral blend includes calcium, magnesium and potassium for muscle and nerve function.
Diet version contains less than 5 kcal per 100 ml, making it suitable for weight management.
Flavorings are derived from natural fruit and berry extracts, without artificial sweeteners.
Packaging is made from recyclable plastic to reduce environmental impact.

items.title: Supports Hydration
items.content: Enriched water speeds up fluid replenishment, especially after physical activity.

items.title: Reduces Fatigue
items.content: Vitamin B12 participates in energy production, helping to lessen feelings of tiredness.

items.title: Supports Bones and Muscles
items.content: Calcium and magnesium aid normal bone and muscle function.

items.title: Antioxidant Protection
items.content: Vitamin C protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Weight Management
items.content: Low‑calorie composition allows quenching thirst without extra calories.

items.title: Allergy to Additives
items.content: Some individuals may experience reactions to vitamin or mineral additives.

items.title: Excess Mineral Intake
items.content: Overconsumption may lead to electrolyte imbalance, especially in people with kidney disorders.

items.title: Medication Interactions
items.content: Calcium and magnesium can affect absorption of certain drugs, such as antibiotics.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Drink 200–300 ml throughout the day, particularly before and after workouts. It can also serve as a base for smoothies or be diluted with unsweetened juices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 5 days.
